`root>low` has `position: absolute` with `z-index: 1`, which makes it establish a stacking context. Its child `root>low>inner` (z-index: 999) is confined within that stacking context — the 999 only ranks it against siblings *inside* `root>low`, not against elements outside.

At the `root` level, we compare the two siblings: `root>low` (z-index: 1) and `root>high` (z-index: 2). Since 2 > 1, `root>high` and all its contents are painted above `root>low` and everything inside it, regardless of the inner element's z-index: 999.

ANSWER: root>high
